description: Verify that after a DHCPNAK in RENEWING the DUT waits a random [1, 10] s before emitting the restart DHCPDISCOVER (RFC 2131 §4.4.1 SHOULD)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 2131 §4.4.1 says when a renewal is rejected, the client returns to INIT and SHOULD wait a random [1, 10] s before its next DISCOVER. The desync prevents synchronized retry storms when many clients lose their leases at once.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DUT runs the full DORA: DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK → BOUND.
2. Tester pushes DUT into RENEWING via T1 timer; DUT emits a renew DHCPREQUEST.
3. Tester replies DHCPNAK to that REQUEST.
4. DUT returns to INIT, then emits a fresh DHCPDISCOVER #2.

[Pass condition]
(t_DISCOVER#2 - t_NAK) ∈ [1 s, 10 s + ParamToleranceTime].

[Fail condition]
• Fail_desync_out_of_range — the wait is outside [1, 11] s
• Fail_no_discover / Fail_no_first_request / Fail_no_renewing_request / Fail_no_second_discover — corresponding DORA / RENEW / restart frame missing

verdicts.Pass: DUT waited random [1, 10] s after NAK before DISCOVER #2 — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within listen window
verdicts.Fail_no_renewing_request: No DUT renewing DHCPREQUEST within listen window
verdicts.Fail_no_second_discover: No DUT second DISCOVER after returning to INIT
